mcp.instructions: Write-only OneDrive tools. get_item fetches metadata (eTag, cTag, size, folder/file, web URL) for a drive-relative path or item ID - it is a pre-write safety check, not a browsing tool; a not-found target surfaces as an error, not a negative answer. create_folder implements mkdir -p: it walks the path from the drive root, creating each missing segment, and is idempotent - an already-existing path succeeds with no changes. create_file creates a new file with inline text content; conflict_behavior defaults to 'fail' and also accepts 'rename' (appends a numeric suffix on collision) and 'replace' (overwrites). Parents are never auto-created by create_file - call create_folder first, or a typo'd path fails loudly rather than silently materializing a folder tree. update_file_content replaces an existing file's content; if_match is REQUIRED (the eTag or cTag from a prior get_item call) - a mismatch means the file changed since that read, and the call fails distinctly rather than silently overwriting someone else's change, so call get_item again for the current eTag and retry. rename_item changes a file or folder's name in place; move_item moves it into a different parent folder, same drive only - cross-drive moves fail with a clear error. delete_item moves an item to the recycle bin, never a permanent delete, and is two-step and confirmation-gated: call once with path_or_id/expected_name/recursive to preview and get a confirmation_token - this does NOT delete anything - then call again with that token to actually delete; expected_name must match the resolved item's actual name, and recursive must be true to delete a non-empty folder. This server may be running in dry-run mode, in which case every write tool - including delete_item's confirm call - validates and resolves but makes no actual change; its response is prefixed '[DRY RUN]' and states plainly that nothing was written, renamed, moved, or deleted. This server has no search tool - obtain paths/IDs from the Microsoft 365 connector's read/search tools, which share the same Graph ID space.
